# Constructed inputs for the set-1626 observer (TestSet1626NeverReachedCorpus): each puts a scalar where indirob can
# complete as indirob ::= scalar, right before a { that might read as HASHBRACK or as a block's PERLY_BRACE_OPEN, the
# one terminal set (1626) whose two terminals get different reduce verdicts after that rule (design §3, §4.1). Each
# input starts at a line "### <name>" and runs to the next; everything before the first is this comment.
### hash element through a scalar
my $r = { a => 1 }; print $$r{a};
### hash slice through a scalar
my $r = { a => 1, b => 2 }; my @v = @$r{qw(a b)};
### key/value slice through a scalar
my $r = { a => 1 }; my %h = %$r{a};
### glob slot through a scalar
my $g = \*STDOUT; my $io = *$g{IO};
### glob slot through a block, then through a scalar
my $g = \*STDOUT; my $io = *{$g}{IO} // *$g{IO};
### code call through a scalar before an anonymous hash
my $c = sub { $_[0] }; &$c({ a => 1 });
### print to a scalar handle, then an anonymous hash
open my $fh, '>', \my $buf; print $fh { a => 1 }->{a};
### print to a scalar handle, then a block
open my $fh, '>', \my $buf; print $fh {; 'x' };
### printf to a scalar handle, then a hash
open my $fh, '>', \my $buf; my %h = (a => '%s'); printf $fh $h{a}, 1;
### say to a scalar handle before braces
use feature 'say'; open my $fh, '>', \my $buf; say $fh {}->{a} // 'x';
### indirect method call on a scalar class with a hash
package Foo; sub new { bless $_[1], $_[0] } package main; my $class = 'Foo'; my $o = new $class { a => 1 };
### indirect method call on a scalar invocant with an empty hash
package Foo; sub new { bless $_[1], $_[0] } package main; my $class = 'Foo'; my $o = new $class {};
### exec through a scalar program name
my $prog = 'true'; exec $prog { 'true' } if 0;
### system through a scalar program name and a block
my $prog = 'true'; system $prog { 'true' } 'true' if 0;
### sort with a scalar comparator before a list in braces
my $by = sub { $a <=> $b }; my @s = sort $by @{[3, 1, 2]};
### element of a deref'd hash, empty braces after the sigil
my $r = {}; my @x = (exists $$r{''});
### array through a scalar, then an anonymous hash
my $r = [1, 2]; my @a = (@$r, { a => 1 });
### array element through a scalar before a hash constructor
my $r = [{ a => 1 }]; my $v = $$r[0]{a};
### print to STDOUT then a scalar then braces
my $x = 1; print STDOUT $x, { a => 1 }->{a};
### return of a glob slot through a scalar
sub io { my $g = shift; return *$g{IO} } io(\*STDOUT);
### glob slot by name after a print to a scalar handle
open my $fh, '>', \my $buf; print $fh *STDOUT{IO} ? 1 : 0;
### constant list after a scalar
my $x = 1; use constant { A => 1 }; print $x, A;
